findings.note: Dead assertion: the open-flag/permission check is short-circuited. The loop fails only when BOTH clauses are false, and the second clause (strings.Contains(o, "-rw-------")) is true for every recorded open because writeFile always passes perm 0o600, so the flag half of the assertion can never fire. Compounding it, the expected flag word is built with the local itoa() at export_test.go:120, which is string(rune('0'+i%10)) - a single digit, so distinct flag words collide; and the literal 0x100 stands in for syscall.O_NOFOLLOW, which is 0x100 only on darwin (0x20000 on linux). Net effect: the security-relevant O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW flags on export.go:222 are never asserted by this test. TestOSFS (export_test.go:553) does cover O_EXCL against the real filesystem, so the production behavior is verified elsewhere; only O_NOFOLLOW is unasserted. Fix: compare m.opens entries against a real strconv.Itoa of the flag word and drop the || fallback.

findings.note: MaxDiffBytes is a mutable package-level global declared purely so tests can force truncation, and its only mutator restores it by plain assignment rather than defer/t.Cleanup. If the assertion between the two assignments fails with t.Fatalf, the goroutine exits with MaxDiffBytes still set to 2 and every later test in the package silently sees a 2-byte diff budget, turning one failure into a cascade of misleading ones. The package has no t.Parallel today, so there is no data race, but a future parallel test would introduce one. Fix: guard the mutation with defer func(v int){ MaxDiffBytes = v }(MaxDiffBytes) or t.Cleanup.
